1.name: January
1.note: The year begins in the tropics, in mixed flocks at good feeding trees.

2.name: February
2.note: Still on the wintering grounds; early migrants begin moving through Panama.

3.name: March
3.note: Some reach Mexico; many are still as far south as Panama.

4.name: April
4.note: Peak migration begins. First arrivals reach Texas; a few reach the central states by month's end.

5.name: May
5.note: Orioles reach the northern states and provinces — peak month for nest-building.

6.name: June
6.note: Most eggs hatch this month; parents incubate and feed young.

7.name: July
7.note: Fledglings become independent; some adults begin migrating as early as the start of the month.

8.name: August
8.note: Migration builds toward its peak, which spans August and September.

10.name: October
10.note: Migration eases in the first half of the month; most reach tropical wintering grounds.

11.name: November
11.note: Mostly in the tropics, though a few linger in northern states and provinces.

12.name: December
12.note: Nearly the entire population is in the tropics.
